key_insight: The paper introduces a hierarchical way to turn sparse episode-level success/failure outcomes into richer transition-level learning signals for online RL fine-tuning of vision-language-action (VLA) policies. This helps the actor learn more effectively than using one flat scalar reward or advantage for the whole rollout.
problem_solved: Online RL fine-tuning of pretrained VLA policies often provides only a single binary outcome per episode, but policy updates need supervision at the transition level. Existing methods compress this sparse feedback into one scalar signal, which can blur different learning objectives and become less informative once tasks start succeeding.
method: Decompose sparse episode outcomes into hierarchical advantage weights instead of a single flat reward/advantage.
Assign transition-level supervision that better distinguishes which parts of a rollout contributed to success or failure.
Use this structured weighting to provide denser, more informative training signals during online RL fine-tuning of pretrained VLA policies.
impact: For practitioners, this can make online fine-tuning more sample-efficient and stable when reward information is sparse. It is especially useful for robot and embodied AI systems where collecting detailed step-by-step labels is expensive or impractical.
